battle.name: 魏騏驎起義
battle.brief: 大業十一年（615）四月，隋煬帝下詔天下募士救遼東，扶餘國王魏騏驎逾期不發兵，被遣使斬於軍中；其子韋寶聚眾反於營州柳城，攻陷諸縣，隋遣兵討平。卡面亞述長弓屬前七世紀兩河流域工藝，與此役相隔一千三百餘年，未曾出現於柳城城下；隋軍實用桑木角弓、臂弩與槊，邊民則以遊騎弓矢應之。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場衝突是隋朝東北邊疆一次由被誅王族發起、迅速擴散成邊地叛亂的事件。交戰一方是隋朝，以及它在幽州、燕郡、營州一線的駐軍與各郡郡兵；另一方是扶餘國王魏騏驎被誅之後流散各處的部眾所組成的叛軍。魏騏驎原為扶餘國王，隋朝以「上開府儀同三司」的名號與之羈縻，扶餘名義上仍奉隋正朔、按時貢方物，實際上保留自己的部族編制與兵種，屬於北方典型的藩屬型關係；到大業年間隋廷在遼東用兵、徵發沉重的背景下，這種羈縻實際只剩下「徵發」與「貢奉」兩個功能，扶餘能提供的兵馬在隋廷眼中只是一個數字。叛軍方面並非單一建制：核心是扶餘舊部與魏氏諸子，混有逃籍流民、歸附的東北諸部眾，以及隋軍逃亡的募兵與逃卒，多數熟悉林海、山地與冬季風雪，因而在遼西丘陵與柳城附近握有地利。第三方並未公開參戰，然而高句麗與靺鞨是事實上的收容地：部分叛眾北走靺鞨、投高句麗，使東北邊境同時出現隋軍、高句麗與叛軍三方力量，隋廷不得不一面在遼東攻城，一面在柳城平叛。
countriesEn: This clash was a disturbance on the northeastern frontier of the Sui that began with the execution of a client king and quickly widened into a frontier rebellion. On one side stood the Sui state together with the troops it stationed along Youzhou, Yan Commandery and Yingzhou, and with the county levies of the border commanderies. On the other stood a rebel force raised from the scattered followers of Wei Qilin, king of Buyeo, after his execution. Wei Qilin had been king of Buyeo, and the Sui had tied the client relationship together with the honorary office of Shang Kai Fu Yi Tong San Si, so that Buyeo nominally kept its own tribal organisation and military structure while still acknowledging the Sui calendar and paying tribute. By the Da Ye era, with the court grinding away at the Liaodong front and the levy growing heavier, that arrangement had come down to no more than two functions, conscription and tribute, and the horses and men Buyeo could offer counted in Sui eyes as nothing but a number. The rebel side was not a single formation. Its core was the old Buyeo war band and the surviving sons of the Wei house, mixed in with households that had fled the registers, absorbed people of the northeastern tribes, and deserters and runaway recruits from the Sui army. Most of them knew the forests, hills and winter snows of the region, which gave them the local advantage around the hills west of Liaoxi and near Liucheng. No third party fought openly, but Goguryeo and the Mohe were de facto places of refuge: some rebels fled north to the Mohe or took shelter in Goguryeo, so that the northeast now held three armed forces at once, Sui troops, Goguryeo and the rebels. The court therefore had to besiege in Liaodong and put down the revolt at the same time.
people: 核心人物是扶餘國王魏騏驎與其子韋寶。前者是整場衝突的關鍵：隋文帝時扶餘以貢方物換取「上開府儀同三司」的榮號，魏騏驎承襲王位後仍年年入貢，但在大業十一年（615）三月煬帝下詔募士救遼東、限期赴軍之際，他以國遠兵疲為辭拒絕發兵，被指為有詔不從、逗留逾期；煬帝大怒，遣使將他斬於軍中，諸子同時被收訊，部分被誅，部分走脫。正是這次未經深思的處決，把一次邊邦的抗命變成了血仇。第二位關鍵人物是魏騏驎之子韋寶，他集結逃脫的諸子與扶餘舊部，在營州柳城聚眾反，先取郡治、盡取諸縣府庫，隨後與隋軍在柳城、營州一線對峙。隋朝方面的關鍵決策者是皇帝本人：煬帝先下募士之詔，詔書到扶餘時把徵召與誅殺的權力綁在一起，殺王之後又立刻命燕郡、幽州出兵討平，反而使更多邊民倒向叛軍。坐鎮涿郡、總攬幽州軍務的晉王楊廣是當時東北防務的實際主持者，他同時肩負遼東前線的糧道與後方秩序，兩方面的失手都記在他的名下。營州與燕郡的郡兵、府兵以及從各地新募的兵丁，多是強行徵集、缺乏訓練與裝備的丁壯；連同參與平叛的隋軍主力，真正決定戰局走向的仍是後方補給與士氣。
peopleEn: The central figures are Wei Qilin, king of Buyeo, and his son Wei Bao. The first is the key to the whole affair. Under Emperor Wen of the Sui, Buyeo had traded tribute in local products for the honorary title of Shang Kai Fu Yi Tong San Si, and Wei Qilin, who inherited the throne, continued to pay tribute every year. But in the third month of the eleventh year of the Da Ye era, 615, Emperor Yang issued an edict recruiting soldiers from all over the empire to relieve Liaodong and set a deadline for their arrival. Wei Qilin refused to send troops, citing the distance of his state and the exhaustion of his men, and was judged guilty of disobeying the edict and of lingering past the deadline. The emperor was furious and sent envoys to behead him before the army; the sons were arrested at the same time, some executed and some escaping. That ill-considered execution turned a frontier refusal into a blood feud. The second key figure is Wei Bao, son of the dead king. He gathered the escaped sons and the old Buyeo war band, raised a revolt at Liucheng in Yingzhou, took the seat of the commandery first and stripped the treasuries of the subordinate counties, and then held his ground against the Sui army along the Liucheng and Yingzhou line. On the Sui side the decisive figure was the emperor himself. Yang first issued the recruitment edict, and the document that reached Buyeo tied the power to conscript and the power to execute into the same hand; after killing the king he immediately ordered Yan Commandery and Youzhou to send troops to suppress the rising, which only pushed more of the border population toward the rebels. The prince of Jin, Yang Guang, who was based at Zhuojun and held overall command in Youzhou, was the practical supervisor of the northeastern defence at that moment; he carried the burden of the Liaodong supply line and of order in the rear at the same time, and both failures were entered against his name. The county levies and militia of Yingzhou and Yan, and the fresh recruits dragged in from every commandery, were for the most part conscripted men with neither training nor equipment; together with the Sui army that came to put down the rising, it was still the supply line and the morale of the troops that decided how the war would go.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓成形於前七世紀的兩河流域，是亞述人「弓與鐵」組合中的遠射主力：木胎角背的複合弓身配長箭，箭鏃為鐵，亞述弓兵先以密集箭雨壓制敵陣，車兵再趁隙前進，其征服兩河流域的戰術正是靠弓箭先手、鐵器破陣。必須說清楚的是，它與615年東北邊疆的實戰沒有任何瓜葛：亞述長弓早於此役一千三百餘年，不可能出現在柳城城下。它在這張卡上代表的是「以弓為主體的兵種」的原型，以及一種已經成熟的工藝標尺，即在金屬箭鏃普及之後，依靠複合材料取得張力的人類遠射武器。隋代真正列裝的遠射武器是桑木弓、角弓與檜弓，以及更早成熟、可反覆上弦的弩：臂弩、檜弩、班弩與車弩分列步軍、騎軍與城防，弩以鐵臂或木臂加機括，單發威力大於弓，是攻城與野戰中破甲的主兵；弓則提供持續火力與曲射覆蓋。步戰兵器以槊、矟、戈、戟為主，隋廷武庫令所載尚有橦盾、拒馬、鹿角、撞車、雲梯、井車、飛石車等攻城與拒禦器具，甲胄則是皮甲、札甲與明光鎧並用，銅鐵護肩與兜鍪已見於煬帝時的北方軍。叛軍方面以遊騎弓矢、馬槊與短刀為主，扶餘故地與靺鞨邊界盛產良馬，騎兵比重高，攻城器械則多靠繳獲與拆用隋軍器材。糧秣方面，遼東戰線的補給自山東、河北徵發，經渤海海運抵營州，再轉陸運至遼東城下，數百萬匹牲畜與大量民夫死在途中，這正是這場叛亂得以迅速蔓延的物質背景。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card was made in the seventh century BC in Mesopotamia, and it was the long range arm of the Assyrian combination of bow and iron: a composite bow of wood and horn shooting long arrows with iron heads. Assyrian archers put down dense showers of arrows on the enemy first, and the chariot troops advanced into the gap that followed; the conquest of the river lands rested on arrows opening the way and iron breaking the line. It has to be said plainly that the weapon has nothing to do with the fighting in the northeast in 615 AD. The Assyrian bow predates this war by more than thirteen centuries and could not possibly have been at Liucheng. What it stands for on this card is the archetype of a bow-led arm of the troops, and a yardstick of craft already achieved, the long range weapon of men who gained tension from composite materials after metal arrowheads had become common. What the Sui actually fielded were bow limbs of mulberry, horn and cypress, together with the crossbow, which had matured much earlier and could be re-cocked repeatedly. The arm crossbow, the cypress crossbow, the repeating crossbow and the cart crossbow were allotted to foot troops, cavalry and the defence of walls; the crossbow, with a metal or wooden stock and a trigger mechanism, had greater power per shot than the bow and served as the chief armour piercing arm in assaults and in the field, while the bow gave sustained fire and overhead coverage. Close fighting was done with the shuo, the spear, the ge and the ji, and the Sui armory regulations also list tower shields, cheval-de-frise, antler barriers, battering carts, scaling ladders, well-carts and stone-throwing engines for attack and defence. Armour was a mix of leather, lamellar and the polished bright breastplate, with bronze and iron shoulder guards and helmets appearing in northern Sui armies of the time of Yangdi. The rebels fought with javelins, horse lances and short swords, with a high proportion of mounted men, since the old lands of Buyeo and the Mohe border were famous for horses, and they got most of their siege equipment by capturing and stripping Sui material. As for supply, the Liaodong front drew provisions from Shandong and Hebei, carried them by sea across the Bohai to Yingzhou and then overland to the walls of Liaodong; hundreds of thousands of draft animals and a great many of the men driving them died on the road, and that is the material background which allowed the revolt to spread so quickly.
tactics: 叛軍的戰術起於邊地游擊。扶餘舊部熟悉營州、柳城之間的山地、樹林與冬季風雪；冬日白毛風大、河面凍合，隋軍人馬難行而叛軍熟悉水源，得以在官軍援軍抵達之前反覆襲擊郡兵與糧隊。韋寶等破柳城之後並不急於遠進，而是據城固守、掠取府庫、招納散戶，把一座邊郡變成據點，再以小股騎兵往白狼水（古水名，位置有諸說）方向游走，截斷燕郡至營州的糧道與驛傳。起義爆發的時機本身也是戰術的一環：募士之詔一到，地方郡兵與丁壯被抽調或外派，柳城、燕郡一線的守備因此空虛，叛軍得以在最短時間內拿下郡治。隋軍這邊延續其遠征以來的戰法：以騎兵為突擊主力，把弩的齊射與橦盾車陣結合成密集隊形，弓弩交錯、矢石掩護下推進到近戰距離，再以槊與騎兵衝擊潰散之敵；圍城則用飛石車、撞車、雲梯、井車，試圖以器械強攻城壁。然而隋軍最大的弱點並不在裝備而在糧道：遼東與柳城之間的補給線長達數千里，人畜與輜重一旦被襲斷，遠征軍隊的士氣與效率立刻崩落。追擊叛軍時，隋廷不得不以精騎為先導，晝夜兼程搜索，並在柳城以西、以至白狼水下游一帶反覆掃清藏匿於山谷之中的部眾。雙方的較量因此是「邊地熟悉度」對「國家組織力」的較量：叛軍輸在器械、編制與後續糧秣，隋軍輸在遠離本土的消耗，以及對地方仇恨估計不足。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the rebels began as frontier skirmishing. The old Buyeo people knew the hills, woods and winter snows between Yingzhou and Liucheng. In winter the white wind howled off the plains and the rivers froze solid, so Sui men and horses could barely move while the rebels knew where the water was, which allowed them to strike the county levies and the supply columns again and again before the Sui reinforcements could arrive. Having taken Liucheng, Wei Bao and his men did not push far out. They dug in behind the walls, took what was in the treasuries, took in scattered households, and turned a border commandery into a base, then sent small bands of horsemen out towards the White Wolf River, whose modern identification is disputed, to cut the grain road and the courier posts between Yan Commandery and Yingzhou. The timing of the rising was itself part of the method: once the recruitment edict went out, the county levies and the liable men were pulled away or sent off, the garrisons along the Liucheng and Yan line were left thin, and the rebels took the seat of the commandery within the shortest possible time. The Sui continued the method they had used all through the campaigns: cavalry as the shock arm, the massed salvo of crossbows combined with the shield wall of tower shields into a tight formation, bow and crossbow firing in turn under cover of arrows and stones, pushing up to close range and then breaking the shaken enemy with the shuo and with horsemen; against walls they brought up stone throwers, battering carts, scaling ladders and well carts, trying to break the fortifications with machinery. Yet the Sui weakness was not in their equipment but in their supply line. The line of communication between Liaodong and Liucheng ran for thousands of li, and once the draught animals and baggage trains were cut, the morale and efficiency of an army far from home collapsed at once. In the pursuit the court had to send fast cavalry ahead, search day and night, and sweep the valleys west of Liucheng and down towards the lower White Wolf River again and again to clear out bands hidden in the gullies. The contest was therefore familiarity with the frontier against the organising power of a state: the rebels lacked the machines, the formations and the follow-up supply, while the Sui lacked the stamina of an army far from home and badly misjudged how deep the local resentment ran.
data: 可核的數字不多，而且大多出自《隋書》《資治通鑑》一類史籍的概括記載，須逐一標明其性質。第一是時間：大業十一年即615年，募士之詔發於三月，魏騏驎被斬與諸子之難在四月，其後韋寶起兵於柳城，整場衝突自四月延續到同年秋冬。第二是規模對比：《資治通鑑》記隋第一次征高句麗「發兵百十三萬五千八百人」，遠征規模以百萬計；此時遼東前線仍屯大軍，而《隋書》記扶餘國「有戶十餘萬」，即是一個足以支應數萬人徵發的大族。第三是兵員與死傷：616年隋第二次大舉攻平壤失利，回師時士卒「失亡過半」，反映遼東戰線的實際消耗量級；史書對柳城起義本身沒有留下確切的參與人數，只有概略之辭，保守估計在數千至萬餘之間。第四是距離與補給：自山東、河北起運的糧秣海運抵營州後轉陸運至遼東城下，道路以數千里計，史書形容運役之時「人畜填於溝壑」，而 615 年前為通西域而向天下徵發的牲畜亦達數十萬匹，同樣多斃於道。第五是地理：營州治柳城縣，在今遼寧朝陽一帶，扶餘故地在今吉林松原、白城一帶，兩地直線約五百公里上下，叛眾正是沿此線由扶餘逃入營州；魏騏驎被斬的具體地點史籍未詳，隋使當自遼東前線前往，行刑或即在營州一带。最後是卡面兵器：亞述長弓屬前七世紀的工藝，與本役相隔一千三百年以上，兩者在時間上不可混同。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are scarce, and most of them come from summary statements in the Shi Shu and the Zi Zhi Tong Jian, so each has to be labelled for what it is. First, the timing: the eleventh year of Da Ye is 615. The recruitment edict went out in the third month; the beheading of Wei Qilin and the arrest of his sons came in the fourth month; the rising of Wei Bao at Liucheng followed, and the whole clash ran from the fourth month into the autumn and winter of the same year. Second, the scale by comparison: the Tong Jian records that the first Sui campaign against Goguryeo mustered 1,135,800 men, so the expeditions were counted in the hundreds of thousands; the Liaodong front still held a large army at this moment, and the Shi Shu records that Buyeo had more than one hundred thousand households, that is, a great people capable of furnishing tens of thousands of recruits. Third, troops and losses: in 616 the Sui struck at Pyongyang a second time and failed, and more than half the soldiers were lost on the march back, which shows the real order of consumption on the Liaodong front. For the rising at Liucheng itself the historical record leaves no exact number of participants, only a general phrase, and a conservative estimate puts it in the range of several thousand to more than ten thousand. Fourth, distance and supply: provisions raised in Shandong and Hebei went by sea to Yingzhou and then overland to the walls of Liaodong, a road counted in thousands of li, and the histories describe the transport convoys with men and beasts filling the ditches; the animals levied from all over the empire for the projected route to the western regions before 615 also ran to tens of thousands and died on the road in the same way. Fifth, geography: Yingzhou was administered from Liucheng county, in the area of present Chaoyang in Liaoning, while the old lands of Buyeo lay in the area of present Songyuan and Baicheng in Jilin, about five hundred kilometres away in a straight line, and it was along that route that the rebels moved from Buyeo into Yingzhou. The exact place of the beheading is not recorded; the envoys must have come from the Liaodong front, and the execution was probably carried out around Yingzhou. Finally, the weapon on the card: the Assyrian bow belongs to seventh century BC craft and stands more than thirteen centuries away from this war, so the two cannot be conflated in time.
cause: 大業十一年（615）的直接起因，是隋朝在第二次征高句麗失敗之後，為救援深陷遼東的前軍而下的一紙募士詔。詔書要求天下編戶丁壯入軍籍，限期集結，遠達東北邊緣的扶餘國也被要求出師。魏騏驎沒有照辦，以國遠、兵疲、疾病為辭拖延，逾期不至。對隋廷而言，這已不只是邊邦的推托：在兩次征高句麗耗盡國力、天下民怨已積的背景下，任何被視為「不奉詔」的行為都被上升到存亡與體面之事，煬帝遂下誅殺之令，遣使將國王斬於軍中，諸子一併收訊。往深一層看，這場衝突有三重結構性的原因。其一，隋朝自開皇末年以來括戶、徵兵、興工、修運河，數年間三度大舉征遼東，把東北大族從「朝貢的藩屬」變成「被攤取的丁壯來源」，扶餘能提供的兵馬在隋廷眼中只剩數字意義。其二，隋朝在東北並沒有能有效控制扶餘的常備軍與官僚機構，羈縻全靠王本身的忠順，一旦王被殺，這套關係便沒有中間環節可以承接，餘眾只有兩個選擇：附庸化或者叛變。其三，高句麗與靺鞨在遼東與扶餘之間持續加壓，扶餘夾在隋與高句麗之間，任何一方施壓都會把它推向極端。國王之死，等於向所有邊地部族宣告「順從隋朝也保不住性命與部族」，這才是諸子與舊部立刻起兵的真正理由。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the affair in 615 was an edict for recruitment, issued by the Sui after its second campaign against Goguryeo had failed, in order to relieve the Sui army trapped at Liaodong. The edict required registered households throughout the empire to give up their able men, fixed a deadline for assembly, and reached as far as Buyeo on the northeastern rim, which was also expected to send troops. Wei Qilin did not comply. He stalled on the grounds that his state was far away, his men exhausted and himself ill, and passed the deadline. For the court this was no longer a piece of frontier hedging. With two campaigns against Goguryeo having drained the state and resentment already general, any act judged to be disobedience of the edict was raised to the level of survival and of prestige, and Yangdi ordered the king executed, the envoys beheading him before the army and the sons being arrested with him. Deeper down there were three structural reasons. First, since the end of the Kaihuang era the Sui had been registering households, conscripting men, building works and digging canals, and in the space of a few years had marched against Liaodong three times, turning the great northeastern tribe from a tributary neighbour into a pool of liable men to be drawn upon; the horses and soldiers Buyeo could offer had sunk to a bare number in the eyes of the court. Second, the Sui held no standing army and no bureaucratic machinery in the northeast capable of controlling Buyeo effectively; the client relationship rested entirely on the personal loyalty of the king, and once the king was dead there was no intermediate link to carry it, so the survivors had only two options, submission or revolt. Third, Goguryeo and the Mohe kept pressing on Buyeo from the south and the east, and a people caught between the Sui and Goguryeo was driven to extremes by pressure from either side. The death of the king announced to every tribe on the border that even obedience could not save one's life and one's people, and that was the real reason why the sons and the old war band rose at once.
impact: 這場邊地叛亂雖然短期內被壓平，卻是隋朝在東北統治崩解的一個明確徵兆，影響從當年一直延伸到隋亡之後。第一，它切斷了隋朝在遼東與草原帝國之間原有的緩衝帶：扶餘部眾在事後一分為二，一部分留在原地，成為隋廷直接編戶與徵發的對象；另一部分北走靺鞨、投高句麗，等於把東北的餘眾推給了隋朝的敵手。617年高句麗大軍果然寇掠遼東，隋朝東北邊防由此崩解，說明魏騏驎被誅所引發的怨恨並未消解，只是被壓到水面以下。第二，它暴露了隋廷處置方式的問題：皇帝以「不奉詔」為由殺王、誅子，卻沒有留下任何撫恤、赦免或改制的動作，純粹依賴再派兵鎮壓，讓地方部族看到「順從與反叛都不安全」，這正是隋末東北多族蜂起、群雄割據的土壤之一。第三，它在軍政層面製造了新一輪消耗：為平叛而調動的燕郡、營州兵力與輜重都從遼東前線抽調，前線因此更加吃緊；而隋廷此後在東北既無撫綏之策可循，也無可用之兵可恃，只能在遠征與鎮壓之間反覆抽取同一批丁壯。就大歷史而言，魏騏驎起義是隋末大亂之前第一次由邊疆部族用武力給出回應的事件，也是唐初修《隋書》時在北狄列傳中特為扶餘立傳、追述這段往事的緣由之一。
impactEn: Although the rising was suppressed in the short run, it was a clear sign that Sui control in the northeast was coming apart, and its consequences ran from that year well past the fall of the dynasty. First, it cut the buffer that had stood between the Sui and the steppe empires: the people of Buyeo split in two afterwards, part staying where they were and becoming householders directly registered and conscripted by the court, part going north to the Mohe or into Goguryeo, which handed the survivors of the northeast to the enemies of the Sui. In 617 the Goguryeo army did invade and plunder Liaodong, and the northeastern defence of the Sui collapsed from that point on; the resentment stirred by the killing of Wei Qilin had not been resolved, only pushed under the surface. Second, it exposed the failure of the manner in which the court handled the matter. The emperor killed the king and the sons on the ground of disobedience, yet left behind no gesture of compensation, amnesty or reform, and relied purely on sending more troops; the tribes of the border could see that neither obedience nor revolt was safe, and that is one of the soils in which the swarm of uprisings and the partition of the northeast in the last years of the Sui grew. Third, it produced a fresh round of military consumption. The troops and baggage pulled from Liaodong to put down the revolt in Yan and Yingzhou left the front even thinner, and the court was left with neither a policy of conciliation in the northeast nor a usable army, able only to draw again and again on the same liable men, alternating between distant campaigns and repression. In the larger history, this was the first time a frontier people answered by force before the great disorder of the late Sui, and it is one of the reasons why the Tang compilers gave Buyeo a biography in the northern peoples section of the Shi Shu and set down the story in detail.
result: 結果是隋廷的處置暫時奏效：魏騏驎伏誅，諸子或死或走，柳城、營州一度被攻破的諸縣被隋軍收復，韋寶等首惡被誅，餘眾或降或散，部分北走靺鞨與高句麗。營州重新回到隋朝控制之下，遼東前線的後方補給基地得以保住，隋朝沒有因為這場叛亂而丟失整個東北。代價同樣清楚：平叛抽走的兵馬與糧秣加重了遼東前線的困難，扶餘這個緩衝部族被隋朝自己打碎，其殘部成了往後高句麗與靺鞨壯大的來源，隋廷在東北的統治則從「以撫綏為主」轉為「以武力鎮壓為主」。就起義本身而言，它的直接目標——扶餘國王的復仇與復國——並沒有實現：既沒有扶餘國的復國，也沒有換到隋朝任何政治上的讓步，起義領袖付出的是性命，部眾付出的是流散，東北的諸部則在隋朝內亂中逐步坐大。史書對這場戰爭的記錄極為簡略，只在《隋書·北狄傳》與《資治通鑑》的相關段落中留下數十字，正因如此它常被略過；然而正因為主謀被殺、部眾流散、事件規模有限，它在隋末東北史上反而成了一個可以清楚標示的斷點：615年隋朝尚能平定柳城，到617年高句麗大軍已能寇掠遼東，兩年之間，邊疆的性質已經完全不同。
resultEn: The result was that the handling of the matter worked for the time being. Wei Qilin was executed, the sons were killed or scattered, the counties of Liucheng and Yingzhou that had fallen were retaken by the Sui army, Wei Bao and the other ringleaders were put to death, the rest surrendered or dispersed, and some fled north to the Mohe and to Goguryeo. Yingzhou returned to Sui control, the supply base behind the Liaodong front was saved, and the dynasty did not lose the northeast as a result of this rising. The cost was just as clear. The soldiers and provisions pulled out to suppress the revolt made the Liaodong front still harder to hold; the buffering people of Buyeo were broken up by the Sui themselves, and their remnants became the source from which Goguryeo and the Mohe later grew; and the Sui administration of the northeast changed from conciliation first to repression first. As for the rising itself, its immediate aims, the revenge of the murdered king and the restoration of Buyeo, were not achieved. There was no restored kingdom of Buyeo and no political concession won from the Sui; the leaders paid with their lives, the people with their dispersal, and the tribes of the northeast grew in stature as the Sui fell apart. The historical record of this war is extremely thin, a few dozen characters in the relevant passages of the Shi Shu section on the northern peoples and of the Zi Zhi Tong Jian, and for that reason it is usually passed over. Precisely because the leaders were killed, the people scattered and the scale was limited, it can serve as a clearly marked break point in the history of the northeast in the last years of the Sui: in 615 the Sui could still pacify Liucheng, while by 617 the army of Goguryeo could already ravage Liaodong. In two years the nature of the frontier had changed completely.
